channel.title: THE SABAEAN UNIVERSE
channel.description: Source-led research on the ancient Horn, DʿMT, Aksum, Almaqah, epigraphy, ancient astronomy, calendar mechanics, and HCM-364.

item.title: DʿMT: What the Evidence Actually Supports
item.description: An evidence-led examination of DʿMT, chronology, political scale, inscriptions, Yeha, regional connections, and the limits of reconstruction.

item.title: Yeha: Monument, Writing, and a Connected Red Sea World
item.description: Monumental architecture, ancient writing, archaeology, Sabaean connections, and Yeha's place within the wider Red Sea world.

item.title: Almaqah in the Northern Horn: What Is Attested?
item.description: Archaeological and inscriptional evidence for Almaqah in the northern Horn, kept separate from later interpretation and reconstruction.

item.title: Reading the Stones: An Evidence-First Epigraphy Method
item.description: A source-first method for inscription photography, transcription, restoration, transliteration, translation, provenance, and historical interpretation.

item.title: From Pre-Aksumite to Aksumite: Break or Continuity?
item.description: Archaeological evidence for continuity, transformation, settlement history, and political development before the mature Aksumite period.

item.title: Aksum: A Red Sea Power in Late Antiquity
item.description: Political power, monuments, inscriptions, chronology, and Aksum's changing connections across the Red Sea world.

item.title: Adulis: The Port Connecting Aksum to the Red Sea
item.description: Port archaeology, maritime exchange, imported goods, highland connections, and the western Indian Ocean trade network.

item.title: Ezana: Kingship, Inscriptions, and Religious Change
item.description: Multilingual royal inscriptions, kingship, military claims, coinage, chronology, and changing religious representation under Ezana.

item.title: Aksumite Coinage: Kings, Symbols, and Long-Distance Exchange
item.description: Aksumite coins as evidence for rulers, portraits, inscriptions, symbolism, chronology, metallurgy, and long-distance exchange.

item.title: The Stelae of Aksum: Monument, Tomb, and Royal Memory
item.description: Monumental stone-working, elite funerary contexts, architectural imagery, chronology, engineering, and royal memory at Aksum.

item.title: The Great Temple at Yeha: Architecture, Cult, and Evidence
item.description: The Great Temple at Yeha examined through architecture, sanctuary archaeology, Almaqah, chronology, Sabaean connections, and evidence boundaries.

item.title: Meqaber Gaʿewa: Temple, Royal Dedication, and Almaqah
item.description: Sanctuary archaeology, royal dedication, Almaqah, provenance, political context, and regional relationships at Meqaber Gaʿewa.

item.title: Royal Dedications: What Ancient Inscriptions Actually Tell Us
item.description: An evidence-first guide to names, titles, divine references, construction acts, restoration, translation, provenance, and royal claims in ancient inscriptions.

item.title: Almaqah: Evidence, Interpretation, and Reconstruction
item.description: Secure Almaqah attestation separated from scholarly interpretation, celestial identification, symbolism, comparison, and HCM reconstruction.

item.title: Visual Epigraphy: Reading Ancient Inscriptions from Images
item.description: Authentic inscription photography, preservation, transcription, restoration, transliteration, provenance, and responsible digital presentation.

item.title: The 364-Day Year: Ancient Calendar Evidence and Mechanics
item.description: Ancient evidence for the 364-day schematic year, including 52 weeks, four 91-day quarters, astronomical limits, and the boundary with HCM-364.

item.title: The Book of Luminaries: Gates, Sun, Moon & Ancient Astronomy
item.description: 1 Enoch 72–82 examined through solar and lunar motion, changing day length, schematic astronomy, and its six eastern and corresponding western solar gates.

item.title: Horizon Astronomy: How Ancient Landscapes Can Track the Sun
item.description: Sunrise and sunset movement, solstices, equinoxes, azimuth, horizon altitude, field observation, landscape markers, and archaeological testing.

item.title: Venus and the Morning Star: Ancient Sky Marker & HCM-364
item.description: Venus as the Morning and Evening Star, conjunctions, brightness, its approximately 584-day synodic period, ancient interpretation, and the HCM evidence boundary.

item.title: Testing HCM-364: Evidence, Astronomy & Research Method
item.description: A research framework for testing the 13 Houses × 7 Gates × 4 Elements reconstruction against astronomy, archaeology, epigraphy, language, chronology, and competing explanations.
